title: Lesson 14: Testing and Verification: Proving It Works Before You Claim It Does
description: Proving agent work by watching tool calls fire, reading real output and exit codes instead of trusting prose, verifying the result in the system, and building a repeatable gate so the work stays proven.

questions.question: Per the lesson about testing and verification, what is the central focus?
options: A review of unrelated code tools
The craft of proving an agent does what you say it does before you claim it to the client
questions.explanation: The lesson turns the claim-versus-result distinction into a method of watching tools fire and verifying results in the system.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the lesson's guidance?
options: A smooth done from the agent is acceptable evidence
Read the command's actual output and exit code, not the sentence the agent wrote about them
An exit code of zero proves the result is correct
A claim is as good as the evidence behind it, and the agent's description of its own work is evidence
questions.explanation: The lesson teaches that a claim is only as good as the evidence behind it, and the evidence is never the agent's description of its own work.

questions.question: Which conclusion does the lesson support?
options: Testing once and calling it verified is enough
Leave the quality check to the agent's memory so it improvises each week
Verify the result by reading it back in the system and comparing it to the source, the way the client's team would use it
Trust the agent's arithmetic because the tool call looked clean
questions.explanation: The lesson teaches the second tier of proof: verify the result in the system against the source rather than trusting the agent's report.
